Elevation and height difference

Drag the terrain to rotate it and scroll to zoom. On a touch screen, drag with one finger and pinch with two fingers. Use the 3D, Top and Side buttons to change your viewpoint.

Open Map & controls on smaller screens. Choose Point A or Point B, then click or tap the contour map to move it. You can also drag a point across the map. The map and 3D terrain use the same elevation model.

Elevation is height above the reference level, shown here as sea level at 0 m. The height difference between A and B is the absolute difference between their elevations. It is a vertical measurement, not the distance along the ground.

Predict the answer to the question, then select Show explanation. Reset restores the starting points and view. Export image creates a still PNG; it does not save an interactive scene.

This is an idealised teaching landscape. Colours show elevation, not vegetation or actual surface colour. The area is 2 km by 2 km. Heights in the 3D view are exaggerated by a factor of 1.4; use the displayed measurements when comparing elevations. The map is always north-up.

This standalone resource contains one lesson. The contour interval is 100 m. Compare contour spacing only when the contour interval and map scale are the same.

The resource works offline in a browser that supports 3D graphics. Resource creator: Cici Yang_NZ. Three.js is used under the MIT licence, included in this file.
